items: Weigh Current Bag: Find your existing litter bag, weigh it on a kitchen scale, and record the weight and purchase price to establish your baseline data point.
Track Usage for 7 Days: Write down every litter addition over the next week without changing your behavior, using a sticky note on the box to capture each refill instance.
Project Monthly Spend: Multiply your 7-day total by 4.3 to estimate monthly volume, then calculate cost per pound and total monthly spend to reveal what you actually pay.
Ask the Anchor Question: Determine whether you're spending more than you're comfortable with or whether the cost is acceptable but the results fall short, because these lead to different solutions.
Score Four Dimensions: Rate your setup from 1 to 5 on odor control, tracking, dust, and maintenance effort to give language to the friction you've been tolerating.
Find Your Anchor Problem: Identify which single dimension, if solved tomorrow, would make your entire litter system feel improved and represents your starting point for improvement.
Pick One Problem to Solve: Select your highest-friction moment rather than trying to fix everything at once, because focusing on your anchor problem creates a clear starting point.
Resist New Purchases: Don't buy anything new until you've completed your audit, because you can't make good upgrade decisions without knowing what you're actually working with.
Accept the Uncomfortable Truth: Recognize that litter isn't your problem — your box design, location, maintenance routine, and room setup are — so you stop troubleshooting the wrong thing.
Evaluate Box Design: Once you've identified your anchor problem, assess whether your current litter box configuration is a root cause of that specific friction point.
Make One Intentional Upgrade: Choose your first gear improvement based on your specific audit data rather than defaulting to whatever product everyone else is using or whatever is cheapest.

Design Around Your Findings: Build your upgrade strategy around the exact issues revealed during your audit, whether that means changing the box, the litter type, the location, or the maintenance schedule.
